To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

habit change interventions should focus on the environmental factors that trigger habit performance, rather than on the beliefs, intentions, or other internal factors that are often the target of interventions.

1) habits are formed by the repetition of an action sequence in the presence of a cue and that 2) the cue can be either an internal cue or an environmental cue; and that 3) once habits are established they are difficult to change; and that 4) habit change interventions should target the environmental cue, and that 5) the most effective interventions to change habits are those that target the environmental cue before habit performance.

habits can be changed through interventions that disrupt the automaticity of the habitual behavior and that this disruption can be achieved by changing the environment that automatically cues the behavior.
